evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: The question is asked of the interviewer and reports prior approach of the field team by community or party actors, so it documents gatekeeping around access to the interview rather than the respondent's own partisanship or perceived influence.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: This item records bodily threat in the specific interview encounter; it is narrower than a general sense of threat and does not record threats reported by the respondent or events in the enumeration area.

Candour is an interviewer's global attribution of the respondent's demeanour during one interview, not a validated measure of truthful answers; it may absorb language, comprehension or social-distance effects from the same encounter.

evidence.quote: must always obey the laws and the courts

claims.text: The forced choice opposes presidential exemption from law and courts against obligatory obedience, so it captures an abstract constitutional stance and not a verdict on any named court ruling or president.

This is a general norm toward military involvement in politics; it is not equivalent to the concrete approval item elsewhere asking whether the army should come in to govern, and endorsement of one need not imply the other.

Oversight of MPs is posed as a normative allocation among president, parliament or council, party, voters and no one; it records who ought to hold accountability, not a report that any overseer actually acted.

The presidential counterpart uses the same fixed option set as the MP item, so a difference between the two offices is measurable only within those offered categories, and the coded option list includes no open-ended other.

evidence.quote: she will be criticized, called names, or harassed

claims.text: The respondent rates the likelihood of community harassment of a hypothetical woman candidate; this is an anticipated social reaction, and it does not report harassment the respondent witnessed or experienced.

evidence.quote: should government and elected officials be doing more

claims.text: The item asks for a desired direction and amount of state effort on women's rights, measured against what officials are doing now; assenting to more effort is an evaluative demand, not evidence that current effort is deficient in fact.

No exact substring check: the stem asks which listed issue is most important for government and society to address, so response is a single capped priority among a closed set, and the option ordering can condition which issue is named as the top one.

evidence.quote: using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates

claims.text: Justification is asked only conditionally on a public health emergency and about a possible measure, so agreement endorses a hypothetical emergency policing power rather than describing enforcement that occurred.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: This records the respondent's belief about survey sponsorship, with survy organization, research company, party, government, God and other as distinct options; misattribution is possible and the field is not an audit of the actual commissioning body.

evidence.quote: Willing to participate in follow-up surveys

claims.text: Follow-up willingness carries a separate not-applicable code for respondents without a mobile number, so the three-valued field cannot be read as simple refusal versus consent across all respondents.

holds.missing: No interviewer identifier, interviewer background or visit-level record among the selected items; the locator's Q111-Q113 exist only outside the supplied packet.
holds.why: Threat and candour reports cannot be attributed to particular interviewers or separated from interviewer composition effects on the cited fields alone.

holds.missing: No wave, country or date field among the selected items, and the bracketed office and place names are unresolved.
holds.why: The constitutional referents and the emergency context cannot be fixed from these fields, so cross-national or across-time comparability of the normative items remains undetermined.

holds.missing: No routing or skip documentation showing whether these gender items were asked of all respondents and whether Q51B was conditioned on a prior answer.
holds.why: Whether the priority choice is an unconditioned response or a routed subsample cannot be established.

holds.missing: No administrative trace of actual survey sponsor and no record of recontact attempts among the selected items.
holds.why: An observed sponsor attribution cannot be validated against the true commissioning body, and stated willingness cannot be checked against later participation.
